facts.statement: The first dinosaurs in Kazakhstan were discovered in 1923 and interpreted by Anatoly Riabinin as hadrosaurids and theropods.
facts.quote: The first dinosaurs were discovered in Kazakhstan in 1923, where they were brought from the South Kazakhstan region and interpreted by Soviet palaeontologist Anatoly Riabinin to be from hadrosaurids as well as theropods.

facts.statement: Geologist Vasilij Prynada excavated the dinosaur horizon near Tashkent from 1924 to 1926, finding abundant fossils along a 20 km stretch of the Alymtau Range.
facts.quote: From 1924 to 1926, the Soviet Geological Committee sent geologist Vasilij Prynada to excavate the dinosaur horizon near Tashkent, where the most abundant fossils were found within a 20 km stretch along the Alymtau Range near the Kyrk-Kuduk well.

facts.statement: Anatoly Riabinin formally described the new taxa Jaxartosaurus and Bactrosaurus in 1939 after informally proposing them in 1937 and 1938.
facts.quote: From these discoveries, Riabinin informally proposed the new hadrosaurids "Jaxartosaurus aralensis" and "Bactrosaurus prynadai" in 1937 and 1938, before formally describing both new taxa in 1939.

facts.statement: Anatoly Rozhdestvensky designated a partial skull roof (PIN 1/5009) as the lectotype of Jaxartosaurus because the original collection contained multiple individuals.
facts.quote: Rozhdestvensky designated PIN 1/5009, a partial skull roof, as the lectotype of Jaxartosaurus due to its diagnostic nature, as the collection PIN 5009 included multiple individuals.

facts.statement: A second species, Jaxartosaurus fuyunensis, was described in 1984 based on a partial dentary from Xinjiang, China, but is considered dubious.
facts.quote: A second species, Jaxartosaurus fuyunensis, was described by Wu in 1984 for a partial dentary from Xinjiang, China, but it is dubious.

facts.statement: Riabinin classified Jaxartosaurus as a member of Lambeosaurinae based on the skull roof, noting it was only the second such dinosaur found in Asia at the time.
facts.quote: Based on the skull roof, Riabinin classified Jaxartosaurus as a member of Lambeosaurinae, only the second from Asia after Bactrosaurus in his classification.

facts.statement: Jaxartosaurus belongs to the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
Rozhdestvensky dated Jaxartosaurus to the Coniacian to Santonian stages based on similarities to other hadrosaurs from better-constrained deposits.
facts.quote: Rozhdestvensky extrapolated that the hadrosaurs from Kazakhstan would be from the Turonian to Santonian based on similarities to hadrosaurs from better-constrained deposits, with Jaxartosaurus being slightly younger, dating to the Coniacian to Santonian.

facts.statement: Jaxartosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 84 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 84 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Jaxartosaurus is estimated to be from 89.8 to 83.6 million years ago, spanning the Coniacian to Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Jaxartosaurus have been found in Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: Jaxartosaurus was likely a herbivore that grazed on low-lying plants.
facts.quote: They were likely herbivores, grazing on low-lying plants.

rejected.quote: Jaxartosaurus (meaning "Jaxartes lizard" after the early name of the Syr Darya) is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur similar to Corythosaurus which lived during the Late Cretaceous.
